title: Committee of Supply – Head S (Ministry of Manpower)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head S (Ministry of Manpower)

sections.label: Fair Consideration Framework introduction
sections.summary: The passage states the journey was arduous but positive, and notes the Fair Consideration Framework and National Jobs Bank were introduced in 2014.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: It has been an arduous, but positive journey.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: We have seen the introduction of the Fair Consideration Framework (FCF) and the National Jobs Bank in 2014.

sections.label: FCF effectiveness update request
sections.summary: The passage asks MOM for an update on FCF's effectiveness in levelling the playing field for local PMEs and eradicating nationality bias in hiring.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: In this regard, I wish to ask the Ministry of Manpower (MOM) to provide an update on how effective FCF has been the past 18 months since the implementation in levelling the playing field for our local PMEs and in eradicating "nationality bias" discrimination in hiring practices, including by employment and placement agencies.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I know the Minister shared that he has nailed 150 companies into what he calls the "watch list" where he sees the "double weak".

sections.label: National Jobs Bank progress
sections.summary: The passage asks about the National Jobs Bank's progress and how MOM and WDA use its data for job matching and employment, especially for PMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: In the same vein, I wish to ask about the progress of the National Jobs Bank and how MOM and the Workforce Development Agency (WDA) have been able to make use of the data to extrapolate the job openings and identify the skills gap to better facilitate job matching and employment, especially for PMEs.

sections.label: MOM tougher for weaker
sections.summary: The passage submits that MOM must make it tougher for the weaker and better for the stronger.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: In short, I submit that MOM must make it "tougher for the weaker and better for the stronger".

sections.label: Frontline staff training and PCPs
sections.summary: The passage says frontline staff should be trained on FCF and Jobs Bank, and asks whether Professional Conversion Programmes can be increased for retrenched PMETs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: In addition, their frontline staff should undergo training so that they better understand FCF and the Jobs Bank.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: Conversely, MOM can also consider rewarding those companies whose staff have a Singaporean Core.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: For example, is there scope to increase the number of Professional Conversion Programmes (PCPs) to help retrenched professionals, managers, executives and technicians (PMETs) to find jobs in growth sectors?

sections.label: Older workers and EP inflow
sections.summary: The passage asks how the Ministry will help older workers save their jobs and what is done to manage EP inflow to complement locals.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In addition, how will the Ministry help older workers save their jobs?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Related to that, what is being done to manage the EP inflow and ensure that they complement, instead of competing with locals?

sections.label: Lean Enterprise Development Scheme update
sections.summary: The passage asks the Ministry for an update on the Lean Enterprise Development Scheme since its September launch and the profiles of its applicants.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: Would the Ministry provide an update on what the response to the Lean Enterprise Development Scheme (LEDS) has been since its launch in September last year?

sentences.speaker: Mr Lee Yi Shyan (East Coast)
sentences.text: What are the profiles of LEDS applicants so far?

sections.label: PMETs among job losses
sections.summary: The passage states that more than seven in 10 who lost their jobs last year were PMETs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: More than seven in 10 who lost their jobs last year were PMETs.

sections.label: Jobs Bank effectiveness for Singaporeans
sections.summary: The passage asks the Minister to update the House on how effective the Jobs Bank is in helping Singaporeans find alternative employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: There is little comfort if Singapore proclaims that we have full Page: 77 employment when, in actual fact, the majority of unemployed workers are Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I would like the Minister to update the House on how effective the Jobs Bank is, in helping Singaporeans find alternative employment.

sections.label: Ban on foreign employee hiring
sections.summary: The passage asks whether MOM would consider a one- or two-year ban on companies employing foreign employees if they list vacancies without trying to employ Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: If such companies list their vacancies in the Jobs Bank without any effort or attempt to employ Singaporeans and instead insist on employing foreign workers on EPs, would MOM consider imposing a one- or even two-year ban on the company from employing any foreign employees?

sections.label: Foreign workers and retrenchment benefit law
sections.summary: The passage says foreign workers should complement the workforce and asks the Government to consider a retrenchment benefit law for retrenched Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: Any foreign workers who come to Singapore to work on an S Pass or EPass should complement our workforce rather than displace our Singaporean core.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: I had, in my Budget speech, asked the Government to consider introducing a retrenchment benefit law to ensure that Singaporeans who have lost their jobs would receive compulsory compensation whilst they reskill themselves.

sections.label: Study on retrenchment compensation
sections.summary: The passage urges the Government to study the matter to be fair to employees retrenched through no fault of theirs and to deter companies from retrenching staff to hire cheaper foreign employees.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: But I urge the Government to study this so that we can be fair to employees who have lost their jobs through no fault of theirs and in the process, allow them some time to find alternative employment.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Biow Chuan (Mountbatten)
sentences.text: It will also deter companies from retrenching their staff just so that they can employ less expensive foreign employees.

sections.label: Manpower problem in economic transformation
sections.summary: The manpower problem faced during the economic transformation phase is of great concern.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The manpower problem faced during the economic transformation phase is of great concern.

sections.label: Declining foreign company investment statistics
sections.summary: EDB statistics show fixed asset investment, total business spending and jobs created by foreign companies declined from 2011 to 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: According to the statistics by the Economic Development Board (EDB), from 2011 to 2015, the fixed asset investment, total business spending and jobs created by foreign companies have been declining.

sections.label: Sectoral Manpower Plans for industries
sections.summary: The Government is developing Sectoral Manpower Plans for 25 industries, with EDB leading seven and hotel, retail and construction among the others.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Currently, the manpower issue which I am most concerned about is the Sectoral Manpower Plans (SMPs) which the Government is developing for 25 industries.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: EDB, which services MNCs, is leading seven; the other three are hotel, retail and construction.

sentences.speaker: Mr Thomas Chua Kee Seng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The remaining 10-over industries have yet to be announced.

sections.label: CSP, PME jobs and training
sections.summary: CSP addresses training and skills upgrading, and the speaker asks MOM about employer participation, mature PMEs on the programme, and eligibility.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: As PME jobs make up more than 50% of the workforce, there will be increasing pressures given the current economic outlook and employment trends to build the depth and the quality of the local workforce for sustainable growth and for Singapore to be able to continue to attract investments.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: As the current employment trends are a result of both cyclical as well as structural changes in the economy, CSP addresses not only wage and employment support but, more importantly, it addresses the critical aspect of training and skills upgrading.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Page: 80 As CSP is now in place for about six months, can MOM share how many employers have participated in CSP?

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: What is the number of mature PMEs that are on the programme and the progress made?

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: Can MOM consider allowing more mature PMEs who have been made redundant to be eligible for CSP by reducing the eligibility period that the PME has been out of work to be less than the current six months?

sections.label: FCF exemption for high salaries
sections.summary: Jobs paying a fixed monthly salary of $12,000 and above are exempted from the FCF, which the speaker says should not be the case.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Presently, job positions paying a fixed monthly salary of $12,000 and above are exempted from the FCF.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: This should not be the case, as Singaporeans should have the chance to be considered fairly for all jobs, regardless of salary range.

sections.label: Foreign staff quota flexibility ideas
sections.summary: Suggestions include treating employers with wholly-owned subsidiaries in different sectors as a group for quotas and giving higher foreign staff quotas to companies employing persons with special needs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: One is to consider giving such employers flexibility to employ foreign staff by considering the employer with wholly-owned subsidiaries in different sectors and consider them as a group in applying the quotas.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Another possible "carrot" is to allow companies which employ persons with special needs a higher foreign staff quota.

sections.label: TechSkills Accelerator Programme
sections.summary: Budget 2016 announced the TechSkills Accelerator Programme as an ICT skills learning and job placement hub, with about 30,000 ICT vacancies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: Can more be shared on the TechSkills Accelerator Programme?

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: It was announced in Budget 2016 that apart from enabling our people to learn new infocomm technology (ICT) skills, it will also be a job placement hub for the ICT sector to enable Singaporeans to seize opportunities in new growth sectors.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: At our last Parliament Sitting, we learnt that the ICT sector will have about 30,000 vacancies to be filled.

sections.label: Reskilling for growth sectors
sections.summary: The passage calls for helping Singaporeans in arrears to reskill in IT-related and other growth sector skills, starting by enhancing and expanding the PCP.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: They end up in arrears for their monthly bills and financial commitments and developing low self-esteem.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: We must help these fellow Singaporeans to reskill, specifically in terms of IT-related skills and other skills needed in growth sectors, such as medical healthcare and technology, gerontology and eldercare, the creative industries and even education and training that also require current IT skills.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: For a start, we can enhance and expand our PCP so that we can prepare Singaporeans for the IT industry and the other growth sectors that I mentioned earlier.

sections.label: Company seeking project engineers
sections.summary: A company sought project engineers for roadwork projects and found it difficult to employ Singaporeans despite offering $7,000 a month.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: The company was looking for project engineers for their roadwork projects.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: He lamented that it was difficult to employ Singaporeans even though the company offered a salary of $7,000 a month for these project engineers.

sections.label: Reviewing training programme eligibility
sections.summary: The Ministry is urged to review eligibility requirements for SkillsFuture and other training programmes to move away from requiring formal educational qualifications.

sentences.speaker: Dr Intan Azura Mokhtar (Ang Mo Kio)
sentences.text: At this juncture, I would also like to urge the Ministry to look into how eligibility requirements for training programmes, under SkillsFuture or otherwise, can be reviewed to move away from requiring formal educational qualifications as a prerequisite.

sections.label: Workers retrained under programmes
sections.summary: The passage asks how many workers have been retrained under these programmes.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: How many workers have been retrained under these programmes?

sections.label: SkillsFuture Earn and Learn places
sections.summary: The passage asks how many SkillsFuture Earn and Learn Programme places are available for polytechnic and ITE students in 2016, and notes the National Jobs Bank.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Can I ask the Minister how many places for the SkillsFuture Earn and Learn Programme are available for polytechnic and ITE students in 2016?

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The National Jobs Bank, introduced in 2014, was created to support FCF and, at the same time, help businesses to connect with the local workforce.

sections.label: Harassment and workplace safety cases
sections.summary: Asks the Minister for Manpower how many harassment and workplace bullying cases were reported since the Protection from Harassment Bill, noting rising fatal incidents.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Since the implementation of the Protection from Harassment Bill, I would like to ask the Minister for Manpower how many harassment and workplace bullying cases have been reported.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On workplace safety, the number of fatal incidents has been on the rise.

sections.label: Eldercare and family care leave
sections.summary: States that companies have not readily adopted eldercare or family care leave and that more must be done to widen adoption.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For years, the Government has been promoting and encouraging firms to provide for eldercare or family care leave.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: However, companies have not readily adopted these leave provisions into their systems.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The issue of an ageing population has been on the national agenda for some time.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But more needs to be done to widen the adoption of elder care leave or family care leave.

sections.label: Special Employment Credit for mature workers
sections.summary: Calls the Special Employment Credit good support and suggests foreign worker levy rebates or lower levies for firms employing workers aged 60 and above.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The Special Employment Credit is definitely a good form of support to ensure the continuous employment of such workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms K Thanaletchimi (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It would be even more incentivising if companies that employ or retain mature workers 60 years and above could enjoy a rebate for foreign worker levy or pay lower levy.

sections.label: NTUC U PME Centre and ECT
sections.summary: Reports 1,420 PMEs used NTUC's U PME Centre services from 1 April 2014 to February this year, about 500 on workplace issues, and asks how MOM preserves tripartism with the ECT.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: From 1 April 2014 to February this year, the National Trades Union Congress' (NTUC's) U PME Centre saw 1,420 PMEs coming to us for our placement, protection, progression and privileges (4P) services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: Of the total, about 500 were on workplace issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: On this note, I am asking, with the setting up of the ECT, how can MOM ensure that the sanctity of tripartism is preserved and that the role of unions in grievance handling, advisory, providing representation for our members are not diluted?

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: I therefore, suggest and submit that the Tripartite Mediation Framework provided under the Industrial Relations Act, which avails union members to resolve three heads of claim, must also consequently have its rules amended and have even greater, wider, deeper ambit, scope and jurisdiction than the ECT which avails all, including PMEs, and with no salary cap.

sections.label: Number of freelance professionals
sections.summary: States that the number of freelance professionals in Singapore as of June last year stands at 170,000.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: The number of freelance professionals in Singapore as of June last year stands at 170,000.

sections.label: Freelancers' top three complaints
sections.summary: Lists freelancers' top three complaints as late or non-payment, no outpatient medical privileges and no work injury compensation coverage.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: Their top three complaints are late payment or non-payment, no provision of outpatient medical privileges and work injury compensation coverage.

sections.label: NTUC legal clinics for freelancers
sections.summary: NTUC and the Law Society have run legal clinics, primers and booklets since 2013, and a study on dedicated freelancer legislation is proposed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: Since 2013, NTUC, in partnership with the Law Society, has started legal clinics, conducted legal primers and even did up a pocket series booklet for them, such as this, to equip them with an understanding of their rights, privileges and responsibilities in partnership.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: I submit that we should do a serious study on what we can do for them through a dedicated piece of legislation like a recent Bill that was tabled in California to protect freelancers, especially when the sharing economy and crowdsourcing are happening.

sections.label: Employment and wage figures
sections.summary: From 2010 to 2015 employment rates for ages 25 to 64 rose to 80.5%, unemployment stayed low, and real wages rose 3% a year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: In the past five years from 2010 to 2015, employment rates for ages 25 to 64 have gone up to 80.5%, among the highest in the world.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: The unemployment rate, at less than 2% overall and less than 3% for locals, is among the lowest in the world.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: Real wage went up by 3% in real terms a year, not just the median wage but the bottom 20th percentile in Singapore.

sections.label: Slower labour force growth
sections.summary: Local labour force growth will fall from 55,000 a year to about 20,000, and foreign workforce growth will also drop by more than half.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: The growth in our local labour force will drop by more than half from an average of 55,000 a year in the past five years to just about 20,000 a year for next five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: Likewise, the growth in our foreign workforce will drop, too, also by more than half, from an average of 55,000 per year in past five years to just 20,000 to 25,000 a year in the next five years.

sections.label: MOM labour policy thrusts
sections.summary: MOM will focus labour policies on industry transformation, building a strong Singaporean Core, and strengthening workforce global competitiveness.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: The only way to succeed is for us to become more pro-business and more pro-worker both at the same time, so that, hopefully, we have a manpower-lean and more productive economy with a strong Singaporean Core.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: This is why MOM will focus our labour policies along three main thrusts: first, to support industry transformation to become more manpower-lean and more productive; second, to build a strong Singaporean Core; and third, to strengthen the global competitiveness of the Singapore Workforce, comprising both local and foreign manpower.

sections.label: LEDS and SME support
sections.summary: MOM and MTI agencies launched LEDS last year to help SMEs with capabilities, manpower and markets, adding capacity expansion through the Automation Support scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: SMEs employ about two-thirds of our workforce, so the Singapore economy cannot become more manpower-lean, cannot become more productive and innovative, if our SMEs are not.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: Hence, MOM, together with our other agencies under the Ministry of Trade and Industry (MTI) family, launched LEDS last year to help SMEs to develop their capabilities, manpower and market, including international market.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: And with the newly announced Automation Support scheme, in addition to capability, manpower and market development, we can now add on one more pillar, which is, capacity expansion.

sections.label: Hotel room growth
sections.summary: The passage states Singapore will see a 20% increase in hotel rooms by 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: It is not a sexy sector, but it is an important sector, alongside many other sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: We are going to see a 20% increase in hotel rooms in Singapore by the year 2020.

sections.label: Adapt and Grow wage support
sections.summary: Adapt and Grow offers wage support of 10% to 40% for employers hiring mid-career PMETs at wages of at least S$4,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: The "Adapt and Grow" initiative will provide enhanced employment support to help Singaporeans, especially the mature PMETs and those affected by redundancy.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: Under CSP, to encourage the employers to hire these mid-career PMETs and at the same time pay them decent wages of at least S$4,000, we offer a wage support of 10% to 40% for the first year of employment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: For the first year of his employment, under the CSP, we will subsidise wages of up to S$12,600 for that year for those older than 40.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: For those who are more than 50, it would be up to S$25,200 for that first year.

sections.label: CSP extended to two groups
sections.summary: CSP is extended to two more groups beyond the mature and long-term unemployed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: To help more PMETs, we have decided to extend CSP to two more groups of people beyond those who are mature and long-term unemployed.

sections.label: PCP healthcare and other sectors
sections.summary: About 370 PMETs yearly joined the healthcare PCP, rising to 600 this year, with PCP extended to more sectors.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: In the last three years, on average, each year, we have attracted about 370 PMETs to join the PCP for the healthcare sector.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: As result, we see a 60% increase in response rates.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: This year, we have about 600 PMETs applying to go through professional conversion, up from the 370 per year in the last three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: We are doing the same for other sectors, such as media and design, going into areas, like game writing and advertising.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: We are also going to extend the PCP to more sectors, especially those sectors that are still hiring and growing, for example, chemicals and pharmaceuticals, logistics and retail.

sections.label: Placing mid-career PMETs yearly
sections.summary: The aim is to place more than 1,000 mid-career PMETs under this programme every year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: Our aim is to place more than 1,000 mid-career PMETs under this programme every year.

sections.label: Salary support and training subsidy
sections.summary: The programme provides 70% salary support of up to $2,000 per month and a training subsidy of up to 90%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: Under this programme, we provide 70% salary support of up to $2,000 per month and a training subsidy of up to 90%.

sections.label: WDA allowance and retention incentive
sections.summary: WDA will raise the allowance from $360 to $600 for 80 hours and give a $500 retention incentive.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: WDA will up allowance from $360 to $600 for the 80 hours.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: At the same time, we will raised our retention incentive, meaning that after the 80 hours, if you decide to settle down with your job, we will give them an incentive of $500.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: E2i, WDA, together with our partners, we have helped over 6,000 PMETs and 11,000 rank-and-file workers a year to get jobs With enhanced coverage and support under the Adapt and Grow initiative, we are committed to help even more PMETs and rank-and-file workers.

sections.label: Studying best-in-class job portals
sections.summary: The speaker is studying best-in-class job portals abroad and intends to collaborate with partners to improve the interface over the next 12 months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: We are now studying the "best-in-class" job portals in other countries.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: We intend to collaborate with leading-edge partners to improve the interface to make it more useful for both the jobseekers, as well as the employers, and we hope to see improvements progressively over the next 12 months.

sections.label: Priority is quick re-employment
sections.summary: The priority is helping people get back to work quickly, promising best efforts with varied options, not no pay cut or job guarantees.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: Therefore, our priority is to help them to get back to work quickly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: We are unable to promise no pay cut or a guarantee of job offers, but what we do promise is our best efforts to help, with a variety of options and the diversity of opportunities.

sections.label: Wafer fabrication plants employment
sections.summary: There are 13 wafer fabrication plants employing 8,000 PMETs and 8,000 operators, with 6,000 of the PMETs being local.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: Today, we have 13 wafer fabrication plants employing 8,000 PMETs and 8,000 operators.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: And of the 8,000 PMETs, 76% 6,000 of them, are our local engineers, local PMETs.

sections.label: Foreigners share of EP jobs
sections.summary: At the national level, foreigners account for 21% of jobs within the EP salary range, currently $3,300.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: Today, at the national level, foreigners account for 21% of jobs within the EP salary range, which is currently $3,300.

sections.label: Foreign-to-local ratios and EP growth
sections.summary: In all other sectors the foreign-to-local ratio is under one to two, and EP growth slowed from 32,000 in 2011 to 9,000 last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: All other sectors, all other industries, the ratio of foreign to local counterparts is less than one is to two, less than one-third.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: We must also bear in mind that the growth of EPs has also slowed down, from 32,000 in 2011 to 9,000 last year.

sections.label: Refining EP work pass processing
sections.summary: Concerned some employers may have violated Employment of Foreign Manpower Regulations, the speaker will refine processing of EP work pass applications.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: I am also concerned that some of these employers may have violated the "Employment of Foreign Manpower Regulations", which require companies to take, and let me quote: "…reasonable efforts to provide fair employment opportunities to citizens of Singapore, including efforts to attract and consider such citizens for employment or to train them and develop their careers and potential in the workplace".

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: We will, therefore, refine the processing of work pass applications for EPs.

sections.label: TAFEP watchlist for employers
sections.summary: TAFEP recommends placing employers on a watchlist because their behaviour deepened the local-foreign divide in the workforce.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: At TAFEP's recommendation, they will be placed on our "watchlist", not because we are anti-foreigner but because their behaviour has added to the deepening of the "local-foreign" divide in our Singapore workforce.

sections.label: TAFEP notices to 100 companies
sections.summary: TAFEP served notice on about 100 companies with a weak Singaporean Core, majority EP share above 50% and weak local PMET commitment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: TAFEP has already served notice on about 100 companies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: These are the outliers in various sectors with a weak Singaporean Core, which is much weaker than the industry norm and all of them have a majority EP share of more than 50% and they display a weak commitment to recruit or develop local PMETs.

sections.label: Suspending work pass privileges
sections.summary: For triple weak companies making no progress, TAFEP can recommend suspending their work pass privileges.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: For those "triple weak" companies with no progress made, at the recommendation of TAFEP, their work pass privileges can be suspended.

sections.label: Human Capital Partnership programme launch
sections.summary: MOM will launch a Human Capital Partnership programme later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: MOM will launch a Human Capital Partnership (HCP) programme later this year.

sections.label: LEDS help for SME transformation
sections.summary: LEDS consolidates government schemes into a one-stop service helping SMEs develop capabilities, manpower and markets, with flexibility in hiring foreign workers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: Changes or transformations are often easier said than done, especially for SMEs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: This is understandable, which is why I launched LEDS to consolidate all the schemes from various Government agencies, to provide a one-stop service to help SMEs transform.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: We will work on three areas to help companies develop capabilities, promote manpower development and explore new markets.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: With the addition of the Automation Support Package, we can speed up the transformation of today, to flourish and grow tomorrow.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: During this transition period, SMEs may require some room for flexibility in hiring foreign workers, and the LEDS programme has taken this into consideration.

sections.label: Expanded employment assistance schemes
sections.summary: MOM expanded all employment assistance schemes to help more workers, including young, old, rank-and-file and PMETs, adapt and upgrade.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Mr Lim Swee Say)
sentences.text: MOM has expanded all the employment assistance schemes to help more workers, including the young, old, rank-and-file and PMETs, to constantly adapt and upgrade themselves as various industries undergo transformation.

sections.label: National employment framework proposal
sections.summary: MP proposes a national employment framework with enforcement powers, noting TAFEP's 4,439 pledge signings against 9,106 manufacturing and 58,784 service establishments in 2014.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To date, 4,439 organisations have signed the employer's pledge under TAFEP but, with 9,106 manufacturing establishments and another 58,784 service establishments in 2014, TAFEP's coverage does not seem substantive.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In order for the Government to effectively manage manpower policies in ensuring the Singapore Core and to enshrine the importance of fair employment practices within Singapore, I propose that a national employment framework be developed and instituted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Muhamad Faisal Bin Abdul Manap (Aljunied)
sentences.text: To enforce the framework, additional enforcement powers to penalise double weak firms for discriminatory hiring practices should be implemented within the framework.

sections.label: SME loan scheme and TACs
sections.summary: MP asks how the Ministry can work with TACs, welcoming an SME Working Capital Loan scheme co-sharing 50% default risk on loans up to $300,000 per SME.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: How could the Ministry work closer with TACs to speed up the take-up rate?

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: I am glad that the Government is introducing a new SME Working Capital Loan scheme to co-share with participating financial institutions 50% of the default risk of loans up to $300,000 per SME.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chong Kee Hiong
sentences.text: Total business loans fell 3.5% year-on-year in January to $357 billion and SME loan growth is expected to be a low- to mid-single digit this year.

sections.label: Legislating flexible work arrangement requests
sections.summary: MP asks whether the Ministry could consider legislating the right to request flexible work arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: Could the Ministry consider legislating the right to request for FWAs?

sections.label: Tepid Work-Life Grant adoption
sections.summary: MP asks the Minister to share reasons for the relatively tepid adoption of FWA incentives under the Work-Life Grant.

sentences.speaker: Mr Desmond Choo (Tampines)
sentences.text: In the meantime, can the Minister also share on the reasons for the relatively tepid adoption of FWA incentives under the Work-Life Grant?

sections.label: FWA and Work-Life Grant figures
sections.summary: MP cites the Minister's figures: 47% of employers with at least 25 employees offered one FWA form in 2014, and the grant covered about 900 employees in two and a half years.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Chairman, according to the Minister, the proportion of employers with at least 25 employees providing one form of FWA stands at 47% in 2014.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: According to the Minister, the FWA incentive under the Work-Life Grant has covered only about 900 Singaporean employees in two and half years.

sections.label: Employee right to apply for grant
sections.summary: MP says giving employees the right to apply for the Work-Life Grant, with employers incentivised by the grant, can overcome employees' inertia to FWA adoption.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh Pei Siong (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: Giving employees the right to apply for the Work-Life Grant to fashion and take up FWAs in their companies, with their employers Page: 102 incentivised by the Government grant to accept, can overcome employees' inertia to FWA adoption.

sections.label: Encouraging flexible work arrangements
sections.summary: Asks what measures encourage more flexible work arrangements in organisations for effective work, productivity and employee morale.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: What measures are in place to encourage more FWAs for people in organisations for more effective work and, hence, greater productivity and higher employee morale?

sections.label: Flexible work arrangements for mothers
sections.summary: Members asked for flexible work arrangements for mothers, especially new mothers, which the speaker says might be counter-productive.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: Several Members in this House have asked for FWAs for mothers, especially new mothers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
sentences.text: I would say that, while well-meaning, this might actually be counter-productive.

sections.label: HR Sectoral Tripartite Committee update
sections.summary: Asks whether MOM can provide an update on the HR Sectoral Tripartite Committee's work on these aspects.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Can MOM provide an update on the work of the HR Sectoral Tripartite Committee in relation to these aspects?

sections.label: Uplifting low-wage workers
sections.summary: Says SMP committees with many low-wage workers need customised approaches, and asks MOM for an update on uplifting low-wage workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: The SMP committees, where there might be a large number of low-wage workers, need to work together to have a more customised approach to meet the needs of low-wage workers in the respective sectors to achieve the desired outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zainal Sapari (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
sentences.text: That being said, can MOM provide an update on its efforts to uplift low-wage workers and the key outcomes so far?

sections.label: Rising workplace fatalities
sections.summary: States workplace fatalities rose from 56 in 2012 to 66 in 2015, with 22 deaths since start of 2016 versus 18 last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: The number of workplace fatalities has been increasing, from 56 fatalities in 2012 to 66 in 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: According to the Workplace Safety and Health Council report released earlier this week, 22 workers have died from workplace accidents since the start of 2016.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: This is more than the 18 reported Page: 105 during the same period last year.

sections.label: SME workplace safety challenges
sections.summary: States most companies are SMEs that may lack resources for comprehensive workplace safety measures, facing expertise gaps and significant financial costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: The majority of our companies are SMEs and they may not have adequate resources for comprehensive workplace safety measures.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: Some of the challenges they face include lack of expertise in workplace safety and the significant financial costs involved.

sections.label: Underemployment and discouraged worker statistics
sections.summary: The Government publishes time-related underemployment statistics and gathers data on discouraged workers who have given up job search.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: For some years, the Government has been publishing some statistics on "time-related underemployment", showing the hours worked versus the hours that the employees are available and willing to work.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The Government also gathers data on "discouraged workers", namely, those who have given up the job search.

sections.label: Contract workers figure coverage
sections.summary: The Labour Force 2015 report recorded 202,000 contract workers, and it is asked whether this captures all contract, freelance or ad-hoc arrangements.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: In Singapore, according to the Ministry's report on the Labour Force 2015, there were 202,000 contract workers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Does this figure capture all those who are on contract, freelance or ad-hoc work arrangements?

sections.label: Measuring underemployed Singaporeans
sections.summary: It asks whether the number of Singaporeans underemployed in this way is being adequately measured.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Are we adequately measuring the number of Singaporeans who are underemployed in this way?

sections.label: Retrenched worker re-employment rates
sections.summary: A Straits Times report gave re-employment rates for retrenched Singaporeans and PRs, PMEs, those aged 40 and above, and NTUC PME Centre cases.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A Straits Times report on 20 July last year reported that 57% of retrenched Singaporeans and Permanent Residents managed to be re-employed within the next six months – 57%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For the PME group within this retrenched lot, only 49% are able to find a job within the same period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For those aged 40 and above, within the same group, the re-entry rate was only 53%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The NTUC PME Centre saw a jump of 265 cases of PMEs looking for assistance in employment and employability – from 253 cases in 2014 to 518 from March 2015 to February 2016.

sections.label: Proposed Temporary Income Shield scheme
sections.summary: A Temporary Income Shield is proposed as an insurance scheme modelled after MediShield to cushion a tough and challenging experience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Azmoon Ahmad (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: To cushion the impending tough and challenging experience, I would like to propose a Temporary Income Shield (TIS), an insurance scheme that is modelled after the MediShield.

sections.label: Silver Support Scheme thanks
sections.summary: The Government is thanked for the Silver Support Scheme, described as a major new feature of the social security system.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, I thank the Government for the Silver Support Scheme, which is a major new feature of our social security system.

sections.label: CPF savings and gender gap
sections.summary: A husband transferring eligible CPF funds to top up his wife's retirement account can yield substantial savings, though a 14% CPF balance gap remains between male and female members.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: The savings enhancement for a couple can be substantial if the husband transfers, for example, some of his eligible CPF funds to top up the low balance Page: 108 retirement account of his wife, which now attracts 6% for the first $30,000, and 5% for the next $30,000.

sentences.speaker: Ms Foo Mee Har (West Coast)
sentences.text: Overall, in Singapore, we are still seeing a gap of 14% in CPF balances between male and female members.

sections.label: Adjusting payouts for inflation
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the Minister will consider adjusting future payout amounts for inflation, perhaps at the start of every term of Government, so support keeps up with the rising cost of living.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: If they were to do so, it will help them better manage their limited cash flow.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chen Show Mao (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I hope the Minister will also consider adjusting the amounts of future payouts for inflation, perhaps at the start of every term of Government, to ensure that the support our needy seniors receive keeps up with the rising cost of living.

sections.label: Working group on migrant workers
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MOM will consider creating a working group with Ministries, Universities and civil society to tackle migrant workers' labour issues.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: Will MOM consider the creation of a working group that includes representatives from the Ministries, the Universities and civil society to tackle migrant workers' labour issues, as the universities can provide comparative jurisdiction knowledge and technical knowhow, and non-government organisations (NGOs) can provide an on-the-ground perspective of how the system functions in reality?

sections.label: Workforce growth decline
sections.summary: Workforce growth will drop by more than half in the next five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Teo Ser Luck)
sentences.text: Workforce growth will drop by more than half in the next five years.

sections.label: LED objectives
sections.summary: LED hopes to achieve a few objectives: quality workforce, manpower-lean, and developing Singaporean Core.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Teo Ser Luck)
sentences.text: LED hopes to achieve a few objectives: quality workforce, manpower-lean, developing Singaporean Core.

sections.label: LEDS consolidating schemes
sections.summary: One advantage of LEDS is that it could consolidate and integrate all the several other schemes into one.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Teo Ser Luck)
sentences.text: Second, one of the advantages of LEDS is that it could consolidate and integrate all the several other schemes into one.

sections.label: Temporary foreign manpower flexibility
sections.summary: Temporary flexibility in foreign manpower policy is provided to help companies within that coordination.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Teo Ser Luck)
sentences.text: Within that coordination, we provide temporary flexibility in foreign manpower policy to help them.

sections.label: Handholding companies through implementation
sections.summary: Companies will be handheld through the whole implementation process.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Teo Ser Luck)
sentences.text: Thirdly, we will handhold the companies through the whole implementation process.

sections.label: Applications from 79 companies
sections.summary: Since the scheme's launch, applications have come from 79 companies across sectors including F&B, construction, ICT and media.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Teo Ser Luck)
sentences.text: Since the launch of the scheme, we have received applications from 79 companies, from a broad range of sectors, such as F&B, construction, food manufacturing, ICT and media, professional services, electronics, hotels, logistics, precision engineering and others.

sections.label: Two years' flexibility for S Pass chefs
sections.summary: MOM provides two years' flexibility to retain S Pass chefs beyond the foreign manpower quota so they transfer skills to locals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Teo Ser Luck)
sentences.text: They want to have that pipeline, but this involves skills transfer and capability development and they need foreign chefs to come to Singapore to transfer skills and knowledge to locals during this transition.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Teo Ser Luck)
sentences.text: So, MOM provides two years' flexibility to retain S Pass chefs beyond the company's foreign manpower quota.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Teo Ser Luck)
sentences.text: These chefs are needed to impart skills and knowledge to local trainees who can take on such better jobs in future.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Teo Ser Luck)
sentences.text: With a pipeline of skilled Singaporeans ready to take on critical roles, these foreign chefs will then be released once the transition has been achieved.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Teo Ser Luck)
sentences.text: In fact, we only appointed the multipliers in January this year and the scheme was only launched late last year.

sections.label: HR Sectoral Tripartite Committee engagement
sections.summary: The HRSTC, formed in September 2015, is developing an HR Sectoral Manpower Plan and has engaged over 150 stakeholders.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Teo Ser Luck)
sentences.text: We need to upgrade their certification process as well.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Teo Ser Luck)
sentences.text: We formed the HR Sectoral Tripartite Committee (HRSTC) in September 2015 and it comprises unions, businesses, the Government and IHLs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Teo Ser Luck)
sentences.text: They are currently developing a HR Sectoral Manpower Plan (HRSMP).

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Teo Ser Luck)
sentences.text: Over the last six months, the HR Sectoral Tripartite Committee has engaged over 150 stakeholders through six different engagement sessions.

sections.label: National HR Professional Certification Framework
sections.summary: One initiative considered under HRSMP is the development of a National HR Professional Certification Framework.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Teo Ser Luck)
sentences.text: Ms Thanaletchimi will, therefore be pleased to know that one of the initiatives being considered under HRSMP is the development of a National HR Professional Certification Framework.

sections.label: Companies offering formal FWA
sections.summary: The proportion of companies offering at least one form of formal FWA rose from 38% in 2011 to 47% in 2014, but getting more companies on board is a never-ending effort.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Teo Ser Luck)
sentences.text: The proportion of companies offering at least one form of formal FWA to their employees has increased from 38% in 2011 to 47% in 2014, but it is a never-ending effort to get more companies on board.

sections.label: Online FWA resource portal
sections.summary: An online resource portal will be launched to give employers and employees one-stop access to FWA resources, with both initiatives targeted for the second half of 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Teo Ser Luck)
sentences.text: An online resource portal will also be launched to provide employers and employees with a one-stop access to resources related to the adoption of FWAs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Teo Ser Luck)
sentences.text: Both initiatives are targeted to be launched in the second half of 2016.

sections.label: Work-Life Grant take-up
sections.summary: Take-up of the Work-Life Grant improved from 287 applications in 2014 to 549 applications in December 2015.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Teo Ser Luck)
sentences.text: The take-up of the Work-Life Grant is improving, from 287 applications in 2014 to 549 applications in December 2015.

sections.label: Right to request FWA
sections.summary: In the UK and Australia the law gives employees the right to request such arrangements while employers may consider and refuse them, and Assoc Prof Daniel Goh suggested a similar arrangement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Teo Ser Luck)
sentences.text: In countries like the UK and Australia, the law provides employees with the right to request such arrangements, but employers also have the right to consider these requests and refuse them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Teo Ser Luck)
sentences.text: Assoc Prof Daniel Goh had also suggested a similar arrangement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Teo Ser Luck)
sentences.text: We need to carefully study the pros and cons of having such legislation in Singapore as being pro-business as well as pro-worker.

sections.label: Wage cuts at age 60
sections.summary: More than 98% of companies no longer reduce wages at age 60.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: Today, the vast majority, more than 98% of the companies, no longer reduce wages at age 60.

sections.label: Re-employment effective date 2017
sections.summary: The tripartite partners agreed the effective date will be 1 July 2017, and the additional 3% wage offset for employers who re-employ workers above 65 will similarly be extended to 1 July 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: The Prime Minister shared at last year's National Day Rally that we will do so by 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: So, again, I am very happy to announce that the tripartite partners have discussed and agreed that the effective date will be 1 July 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: The additional wage offset of 3% for employers who re-employ workers above 65 will similarly be extended to 1 July 2017.

sections.label: Amending law for re-employment obligations
sections.summary: The law will be amended to let a new employer take on the original employer's re-employment obligations, subject to the employee's agreement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: Unfortunately, the existing law does not provide for this.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: We will, therefore, amend the law to allow a new employer to take on the re-employment obligations of the original employer, subject to the employee's agreement.

sections.label: EAP amounts and age coverage
sections.summary: Tripartite partners agreed to increase EAP amounts and age coverage in line with the raised re-employment age.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: In line with the raising of the re-employment age, the tripartite partners agreed to increase the EAP amounts and age coverage accordingly.

sections.label: WIS and WTS enhancements
sections.summary: The WIS and WTS schemes will be enhanced in 2017 to support low-wage Singaporean workers who work and train.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: The Workfare Income Supplement (WIS) scheme has been instrumental in encouraging lower-wage Singaporean workers to continue working.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: As announced by the Minister for Finance in his Budget speech, the WIS and WTS schemes will be enhanced in 2017 to provide more support for our low-wage Singaporean workers who work and train.

sections.label: PWM for cleaning sector
sections.summary: PWM has been fully implemented for the cleaning sector since 1 September 2015, covering about 40,000 resident outsourced cleaners as of January 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: PWM has been fully implemented for the cleaning sector since 1 September 2015.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: As of January 2016, about 40,000 resident outsourced cleaners are covered by this scheme.

sections.label: Real income growth of citizens
sections.summary: Over the last five years, real incomes of full-time employed Singapore Citizens at the 20th percentile grew by 2.9% per annum.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: Over the last five years, real incomes of full-time employed Singapore Citizens at the 20th percentile grew by 2.9% per annum in real terms.

sections.label: Dialogue sessions with industry management
sections.summary: The speaker started dialogue sessions with top management from industries with higher workplace injury and fatality rates.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: Recently, I started a series of dialogue sessions with top management from various industries, starting with those that have higher workplace injury and fatality rates.

sections.label: WSH help, recognition and penalties
sections.summary: The passage states that schemes will assist those needing help, good WSH performers will be recognised, and companies flouting safety rules will face stiff penalties.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: For those who need help to improve, we will assist them through different schemes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: As pointed out by Ms Thanaletchimi, we will also recognise those companies which have achieved good WSH performance because we want to hold them up as good role model for others to emulate.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: However, if companies do not take WSH seriously and flout the safety rules indifferently despite warning and advice, we will come down hard on them through stiff penalties.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: Mr Melvin Yong is right in pointing out that some SMEs need more help with WSH training and capability building.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Sam Tan Chin Siong)
sentences.text: We will, therefore, be launching many programmes this year that specifically cater to them.

sections.label: Employment Claims Tribunal and FCF advertising
sections.summary: The passage states the Employment Claims Tribunal will be set up early next year, with a higher claims cap where unions are involved, and that all jobs face fair consideration.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: On the Employment Claims Tribunal raised by Mr Patrick Tay, we will set up the Employment Claims Tribunal early next year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: I want to assure Mr Patrick Tay that we are equally mindful of preserving the role of tripartism in dispute resolution.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Therefore, we will build in a higher claims cap in certain situations where the unions are involved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: On the FCF Advertising Requirements raised by Ms Thanaletchimi and Mr Chong Kee Hiong, I want to clarify that even though the FCF requirements for job advertisements is capped at $12,000 but all jobs, regardless of salaries, including those above $12,000 are also subjected to fair consideration.

sections.label: Singapore time-related underemployment rate
sections.summary: The passage states that in the latest report, Singapore's time-related underemployment rate was 2.9% by June 2015.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: In the latest report, Singapore's time-related underemployment rate was 2.9% by June 2015.

sections.label: Retrenchment benefits survey findings
sections.summary: The passage states that according to the latest survey, nine in 10 retrenching companies paid retrenchment benefits and nine in 10 retrenched workers received them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: According to our latest survey, nine in 10 of the retrenching companies paid retrenchment benefits, and for the retrenched workers, likewise, nine in 10 received retrenchment benefits, including those from the non-unionised companies.

sections.label: Employment Act review and retrenchment benefits
sections.summary: The passage states the recent Employment Act review concluded employers, employees and unions should keep flexibility to negotiate this, and that nine in 10 retrenching companies paid retrenchment benefits.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: The last time was at the recent review of the Employment Act and they came to the conclusion that it is important to allow the employers, employees and unions to continue to have the flexibility to negotiate this rather than prescribing it in the law.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: As I had mentioned earlier, according to our labour survey, nine out of 10 retrenching companies did pay retrenchment benefits.

sections.label: Wage credit for older workers
sections.summary: The passage states that a wage credit to firms is believed to be a better way to incentivise employers to hire and keep more older workers than a foreign worker levy discount.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: A wage credit to firms, we believe, is a better way to incentivise the employers to hire more older workers and to keep them, rather than to give them a discount in foreign worker levy.

sections.label: CPF transfer and top-ups
sections.summary: Regulation was amended to let more members transfer CPF between couples by lowering qualifying savings to the basic retirement sum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Ms Foo Mee Har raised the topping up of CPF and the automatic transfer of CPF between couples to enable them to enjoy higher returns on CPF savings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: That is the reason why we have amended the regulation to enable more members to do that kind of transfer like lowering the qualifying savings from the full retirement sum to the basic retirement sum.

sections.label: Payout inflation adjustment cost
sections.summary: The scheme, introduced in July this year, will cost about $320 million in total budget.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Mr Chen also asked whether we can adjust the payouts to adjust for inflation and so on.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: This scheme, when it is introduced in July this year, the total budget will cost about $320 million, which is not a small sum.

sections.label: Insolvency and unpaid wages
sections.summary: The Minister for Law said liquidation proceeds go to employees second only to the liquidator, and MOM encourages seeking help for unpaid wages early.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: At that time, the Minister for Law replied to Mr Zainal Sapari that when a company becomes insolvent, the proceeds from liquidation are preferably paid to employees who are second only to the liquidator.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: MOM is committed to protecting the employment rights and interests of the workers, and the Ministry encourages all employees probably to seek assistance for unpaid wages as soon as possible before companies reach the stage of liquidation.

sections.label: Retirement and re-employment ages
sections.summary: Workers are protected by retirement age 62, re-employment age 65, and 67 next year; removing retirement age would mean less protection.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Today, workers are protected under the retirement age of 62, re-employment age of 65 and by next year, it will be 67.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: I believe that if we were to remove retirement age completely, it will be less protection for the workers, rather than more protection for the workers.

sections.label: Retrenchment matching and market role
sections.summary: The Ministry matches retrenched workers through initiatives and plugs market gaps; the speaker asks if HR agencies can take on this role.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan
sentences.text: The Minister had explained that the Ministry is taking in the labour market to deal with certain large numbers of cases of retrenchment where the Ministry has stepped in to match the cases of retrenched workers based on different initiatives that the Ministry has thrown up.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan
sentences.text: I think that this is very good and I urge the Ministry to continue doing it.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan
sentences.text: But in specific cases where his Ministry has identified gaps in the market, the reasons why the matching cannot take place, his Ministry has been able to plug those gaps.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan
sentences.text: Will his Ministry, therefore, be seeing to it that the market can ultimately take on this role, such as HR agencies, can ultimately take on this role, so that the Page: 124 Ministry can continue to be active on other areas?

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Randolph Tan
sentences.text: The second question really is to reflect my concerns that we should not let the pendulum swing to the other extreme and then see a certain wave of criminalisation of employers.

sections.label: Task force on retrenchment
sections.summary: Whenever a notice of retrenchment is received, a task force will move in.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: For example, right now, whenever we receive a notice of retrenchment, a task force will actually move in.

sections.label: Private placement companies as partners
sections.summary: The aim is to engage more private placement companies as partners to help place retrenched workers, especially PMETs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Progressively, we want to engage more of these private placement companies to be our partners, so that when there is a retrenchment exercise, especially for PMETs, we can get them to help us, too, to place them.

sections.label: MOM balancing business and workers
sections.summary: MOM is mindful of striking a balance between being pro-business and pro-worker, as both ways alone will not enable growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: So, both ways will not enable us to succeed in our growth.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: That is the reason why MOM is very mindful that we will always strike a balance between being pro-business and pro-worker.

sections.label: Action against outliers
sections.summary: Outliers are being engaged and action is taken against them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: What we are doing is that we are taking all these outliers, engage them and take action against them.

sections.label: Safety nets for workers
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether safety nets such as redundancy or unemployment insurance remain for workers who do not fit schemes like PCP and CSP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: For example, he may have his own contacts to explore, or he may want to become an entrepreneur and so on.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: I wonder if the Minister could give his views on whether there is still a place for some safety nets for these workers who may not fit so quickly into your schemes, such as PCP and CSP.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: In fact, these may not be the best thing for them.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: That there is actually a place, perhaps, for some safety nets for such workers, in the form of some sort of redundancy or unemployment insurance.

sections.label: PCP converting to entrepreneur
sections.summary: The idea was whether PCP could also allow someone to be converted from a profession to become an entrepreneur.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: His idea was whether under our PCP, besides converting a person from one profession to another, or within a sector, whether we can also allow someone to be converted from a profession to become an entrepreneur.

sections.label: Priority is returning to work
sections.summary: Given low long-term unemployment and high retrenchment benefit payouts, the priority is helping workers return to work quickly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lim Swee Say
sentences.text: Our belief is that right now, given the context that we have, low long-term unemployment, high incidence rate of paying retrenchment benefits, I think our priority right now is to help them to go back to work as quickly as possible.
